rationale: C15 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It uses the same distinctive formulation that the lands are “no longer fully needed for military purposes,” restores nearby Waianae military-reservation parcels to the “possession, use, and control” of Hawaii subject to a later limitation, and concludes with an effectively identical reservation of federal ingress, egress, and regress for armed-forces maneuvers. C01 and C03 share the general restoration structure and much literal language, but neither matches the child’s limiting-condition machinery as closely as C15.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the hereinafter-described parcels of such land are no longer fully needed for military purposes
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the hereinafter-described parcels of such land are no longer fully needed for military purposes

shared_material.child_excerpt: Subject to the reservation hereinafter stated, the following-described parcels of land comprising portions of the Lualualei Military Reservation ... are hereby restored to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Subject to the condition stated in the last paragraph of this order, the following-described parcels of land comprising portions of the Waianae-Kai Military Reservation ... are hereby restored to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii
shared_material.explanation: Parallel operative sentence and sequence, with the reservation adapted to a different military reservation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: There is reserved unto the United States the right of ingress, egress, and regress over and upon the subject property for armed-forces maneuver purposes.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is hereby reserved to the United States the right of ingress, egress, and regress over and upon the said tracts of land for armed-forces maneuver purposes.
shared_material.explanation: Nearly verbatim, distinctive reservation clause supplying the same substantive administrative machinery.
